prompt: What is the greatest solution to $2x^2 - 8x = 0$?
hint: Before using any formula, check whether the two terms share a factor. Factoring is the fastest route when there is no constant term.

hints.text: Before using any formula, check whether the two terms share a factor. Factoring is the fastest route when there is no constant term.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a smaller one: $x^2 - 3x = 0$ factors to $x(x - 3) = 0$, so $x = 0$ or $x = 3$. Pull out the common factor and read both roots — never divide the $x$ away.
Both terms contain $2x$, so write the equation as $2x(x - 4) = 0$. Set each factor equal to zero to find both solutions.
The solutions are $x = 0$ and $x = 4$, so the greatest solution is $4$.

learningObjective: Solve a quadratic by factoring out a common monomial.
explanation: Both terms share the factor $2x$, so factor it out: $2x^2 - 8x = 2x(x - 4)$.
A product equals zero only when a factor equals zero, so $2x = 0$ or $x - 4 = 0$.
These give $x = 0$ and $x = 4$, so the greatest solution is $4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pull out the constant first if it helps
steps: Take out the number factor first, then the shared variable: $2x^2 - 8x = 2(x^2 - 4x) = 2 \cdot x \cdot (x - 4)$.
The factor $2$ is never zero, so the product is zero only when $x = 0$ or $x - 4 = 0$.
The solutions are $0$ and $4$, and the greatest one is $4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Dividing both sides of $2x^2 = 8x$ by $x$ leaves $2x = 8$ and silently throws away the solution $x = 0$.
Factoring instead, $2x(x - 4) = 0$, keeps both solutions, $x = 0$ and $x = 4$.
Here the greatest solution is still $4$, but a question asking for the least one would have been missed.
